method.source: Generated docs/ HTML and CSS, all pages derived from CATEGORIES and POLICIES; local byte sizes read from exact referenced files.
method.included: Full HTML, linked stylesheets/scripts, every image occurrence including lazy images and all manufacturer logos, CSS URL resources, and all declared favicon/apple-touch icons. Inline SVG is already part of HTML.
method.excluded: Font payloads, Open Graph/JSON-LD image metadata that browsers do not fetch for page rendering, ordinary link destinations, HTTP headers and TLS/protocol overhead.
method.mobileModel: 390 CSS pixels at DPR 2; parse sizes and srcset width/density descriptors; select first supported picture format (AVIF and WebP), then smallest adequate candidate or largest available; count each selected URL once across the full page.
method.worstCandidateBound: For each image occurrence select the largest byte file among all picture sources, img srcset and fallback src, independent of viewport or format. Count repeated image occurrences separately to avoid understating scenarios where different candidates are downloaded. This is a deliberately conservative upper bound, not an observed transfer or a claim all variants load.
method.compression: uncompressedBodyBytes is exact raw file-body bytes for the model. gzipTextBodyBytes uses Node gzipSync defaults only for HTML/CSS/JS/SVG; raster images remain exact file sizes. Gzip results are estimates conditional on server compression, not measured CDN transfers.
method.networkAudit: Lighthouse network numbers are navigation observations; they do not prove the complete page after lazy loading.

findings.interpretation: All four modeled, deduplicated full-page scenarios stay below 350,000 file-body bytes if HTML/CSS/JS/SVG are gzip-compressed. Modern 390px DPR 2 stays below 350,000 even without compression. Home and Smart Home exceed 350,000 raw bytes in DPR 3 mobile and desktop DPR 2 models. The independent largest-candidate-per-occurrence upper bound exceeds 350,000 on Home and Smart Home even with gzip; this bound deliberately overcounts repeated images and is not an observed visitor load. Lighthouse does not establish an unconditional all-device full-page limit of 350KB.
